content:
We've heard plenty about Apple's next-generation iPad mini, including the inclusion of an OLED display and improved waterproofing.

The latest leak suggests the upcoming iPad mini will be powered by a powerful A20 Pro chip.

MacRumors today discovered references to the new iPad mini within Apple's code, including what appears to be a product icon for the device.

The icon reveals that the overall design of the new iPad mini will remain consistent with the existing model. However, the camera has been repositioned from the top bezel to the side in landscape orientation, aligning with the design of other iPad models. There is also a small speaker grille visible at the top of the display, similar to the iPhone.

The code also indicates that the new iPad mini will feature the A20 Pro chip, the same one used in the iPhone 18 Pro series launched last month. The current iPad mini, released in October of last year, is equipped with Apple's A17 Pro chip.

According to Mark Gurman, the new iPad mini is expected to be officially announced by the end of October. In addition to the changes mentioned above, the new device is also reported to feature further improvements to its waterproofing capabilities and an entirely new speaker system.

For more details, you can check out our complete iPad mini preview roundup.

A separate independent report today also revealed the specifications of the next-generation base-model iPad, including the A19 chip, 8GB of RAM, and Apple's proprietary N1 and C1X connectivity chips.
